title: Replying to @johnsweeney576 #immersive #theatre #experience #sleepnom...
transcript: this immersive Alice in Wonderland show set in a hospital was better than Sleep No More at least in some ways welcome to another episode of Overthinking Theatre Throwback where I do retrospectives on recent theatre history so it's no secret that sleep no more created by the British company Punchdrunk was a massive landmark achievement with immeasurable impact not just on the art form of immersive theatre but in helping to ignite a widespread public interest in it but there's another company that already existed in some form before Sleep No More arrived like a tidal wave on the shores of American theatre but in its wake Third Rail projects rose to prominence with their flagship show, Then She Fell the creators of Third Rail Tom Pearson, Zach Morris and Jennine Willett had their own inspirations behind then she fell synthesizing it from some of their past work with dance and sites-specific installation pieces inspired by Lewis Carroll But the show still felt in multiple ways like a response to Sleep No more where in Sleep no more you often had overcrowded audiences aggressively competing for intimate one on one interactions with the actors then she fell had only 15 audience members per night and was curated so that basically the whole experience was made up of one on ones or small group interactions it was kind of the best of both worlds where you still had a little bit of freedom to open drawers and things like that and the experience was still highly individualized in the sense that not every audience member would experience the same things but the more guided nature also allowed them to ensure that they conveyed the larger story, concept, and themes to every audience member through carefully placed hints whereas one of my big issues with sleep no more and experiences like it is that you could theoretically go the whole show without getting any coherent sense of a story no one can match sleep no more for its scale of course but remember we're not just talking about immersive experiences we're talking about immersive theatre and for my money the Third Rail approach is much more effective at immersive storytelling but what actually is the story? well like I said the show is inspired by Alice in Wonderland but takes place in a kind of mental hospital it was originally performed at what used to be a Greenpoint hospital before reopening in this building that used to be a religious school the show took place around this entire building and as we moved through it we encountered not only the characters from Wonderland but Lewis Carroll himself through these fragmented hints we come to realize that the show is largely exploring Lewis Carroll's relationship with Alice Liddell the real life girl who inspired his title character and while it's up to interpretation we maybe also get the sense that he is a patient at this mental institution and is perhaps populating the building with the characters from his imagination the aesthetic of the show did have some similarities to Sleep No more from its eerie vintage feel its art installation like rooms and its movement driven storytelling and that maybe invited more comparisons between the shows than is ideal but it also had its own brand of hypnotic, almost poetic beauty that did feel distinct from the more brooding melodrama of Sleep No More it also had the fun added element of alcoholic “elixirs” which were not only included with your ticket price but incorporated into the storytelling it was a show that truly stimulated all five senses and many of these moments are really burned into my brain from the intricate and dynamic cup choreography in the Mad Tea Party in the attic to this moment of Lewis Carroll submerging his feet in a pool of water between the broken floorboards Third Rail projects followed up then she fell with the Grand Paradise about a magical spa where time stands still I enjoyed Grand Paradise almost as much as then she fell and for me at least it truly cemented Third Rail projects as a top tier  immersive company with their own strengths completely independent of Punchdrunk I went on to experience three more of their shows including Ghost Light which was performed in and around the Clare Tow Theatre at Lincoln Center a production of a Midsummer Night's Dream that incorporated a food tasting and in 2021 an at home interactive zoom experience where you fold this little paper sculpture as they tell you a story Third Rail is still very much in existence though their presence in New York has been a bit diminished recently not least because then she fell was sadly one of the many casualties of the 2020 theatre shutdowns closing its doors permanently in 2020 after an impressive 8 years
